verdict.fact_pattern_summary: A freelance developer was obligated to deliver a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software artifact meeting committed acceptance criteria. The claimant submitted a self-describing delivery record that explicitly stated it was not independently verifiable. The respondent submitted evidence conceding that CI status alone is not proof of performance. No party produced independently authenticated repository, commit, file, or deployment evidence.
verdict.holding: A commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software delivery obligation is not satisfied by self-describing documentation or CI status alone; the developer must supply independently verifiable proof of repository identity, pinned commit, changed files, and acceptance-criteria satisfaction.
verdict.legal_issue: Whether a developer has satisfied a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software delivery obligation when no independently verifiable proof of repository identity, pinned commit, changed files, and acceptance-criteria satisfaction has been produced.
verdict.reasoning_rule: Under a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated delivery clause, the burden is on the developer to produce independently verifiable evidence covering (1) repository identity, (2) immutable pinned commit, (3) changed files, and (4) reachable deployment artifact or equivalent acceptance-criteria satisfaction. Self-describing markdown, narrative summaries, or CI pass status, standing alone, do not discharge this burden regardless of which party submits them. Failure to produce such evidence warrants revision_required rather than a finding of breach, preserving the developer's opportunity to cure with proper proof.
verdict.short_reason: Neither party produced independently verifiable proof of the commit-pinned artifact. Claimant's own evidence admits documentation is insufficient; respondent's verified evidence concedes CI status is not proof. Both CASE_1 and CASE_2 require independently verifiable evidence, which is absent here, so revision is required.

dispute.claim_summary: The developer did not satisfy the committed delivery obligation with independently verifiable evidence.

relevant_cases.risk: High precedential weight (strength 95) supporting revision_required; directly mirrors the current evidentiary failure.
relevant_cases.shared_issue: Whether a software delivery obligation is satisfied without independently verifiable proof of the specific commit and artifact; descriptive documentation alone is insufficient.

relevant_cases.risk: Strong supporting precedent (strength 86) with identical outcome; slightly broader fact pattern than CASE_2 but materially aligned.
relevant_cases.shared_issue: Whether delivery of a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated artifact is proven absent independently verifiable evidence of repository identity, pinned commit, and acceptance criteria satisfaction.

precedent_search.search_summary: Both candidate cases are materially relevant: each holds that descriptive documentation alone cannot satisfy a committed software delivery obligation without independently verifiable proof of the repository, commit, and acceptance criteria, matching the current dispute's claim and supporting a require_revision outcome.

dispute.response_summary: The developer relies on the committed source and requests independent assessment.

verdict.fact_pattern_summary: A freelance developer was obligated to deliver a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software artifact meeting committed acceptance criteria. The claimant submitted a self-describing delivery record that explicitly stated it was not independently verifiable. The respondent submitted evidence conceding that CI status alone is not proof of performance. No party produced independently authenticated repository, commit, file, or deployment evidence.
verdict.holding: A commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software delivery obligation is not satisfied by self-describing documentation or CI status alone; the developer must supply independently verifiable proof of repository identity, pinned commit, changed files, and acceptance-criteria satisfaction.
verdict.legal_issue: Whether a developer has satisfied a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated software delivery obligation when no independently verifiable proof of repository identity, pinned commit, changed files, and acceptance-criteria satisfaction has been produced.
verdict.reasoning_rule: Under a commit-pinned, repository-authenticated delivery clause, the burden is on the developer to produce independently verifiable evidence covering (1) repository identity, (2) immutable pinned commit, (3) changed files, and (4) reachable deployment artifact or equivalent acceptance-criteria satisfaction. Self-describing markdown, narrative summaries, or CI pass status, standing alone, do not discharge this burden regardless of which party submits them. Failure to produce such evidence warrants revision_required rather than a finding of breach, preserving the developer's opportunity to cure with proper proof.
verdict.short_reason: Neither party produced independently verifiable proof of the commit-pinned artifact. Claimant's own evidence admits documentation is insufficient; respondent's verified evidence concedes CI status is not proof. Both CASE_1 and CASE_2 require independently verifiable evidence, which is absent here, so revision is required.
